operator_io_quirks: All identifiers lowercase, no spaces; still double-quote in generated SQL per spec.

person (128854) and games_competitor (180252) and competitor_event (260971) exceed 300k? No: all <300k, but person_region 130521 and competitor_event 260971 are large; rowid%k sampling still applies for safety.
All declared types are INTEGER or TEXT; no Date/Time/Bool/Bit/Year dispatch, no crash-fallback types.
games_year is INTEGER but semantically a year (1900-2012); TS Number fuzzer will emit values in [-10^0,10^0]? No: scale=0 -> [-1,1] plus perturbations, wildly implausible years.
height/weight INTEGER with 0 present (missing sentinel); TS Number will emit negatives and tiny values.
age INTEGER 0..~74; TS Number scale=0 gives [-1,1] range -> implausible ages.
games_city, person_region, competitor_event have NO primary key (pk=[]); TS sample_fresh_primary_keys is a no-op there, so duplicate rows survive.
games_city.games_id distinct=51 but rows=52 -> one duplicate pair exists; person_region has 130521 rows over 128854 persons -> many-to-many duplicates.
competitor_event.medal_id distinct=4 (1..4) with medal table 4 rows; FK to medal is fine but medal_id NULL rate 0 while column is nullable.
noc_region.region_name distinct=230 < rows=231 -> one duplicate region name; not unique-constrained.
All FKs point to existing parents with unique PKs; no dangling FKs, no self-references, no composite keys.
season and gender are 2-value TEXT enums; TS String fuzzer will emit random charset strings, destroying the enum.
operator_ts_expectations: Every column dispatches to Number (INTEGER) or String (TEXT); no Date/Time/Bool fuzzers exercised.

Number fuzzer with scale=0: fresh draws uniform in [-1,1] then +-1/+-2 perturbation -> id, games_year, height, weight, age all get tiny/negative values; PK ids collide heavily -> sample_fresh_primary_keys drops most rows, shrinking tables far below chosen size.
String fuzzer: random 0-20 char strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() plus contamination; city_name, full_name, event_name, sport_name become gibberish; season/gender/medal_name/noc lose their enum semantics.
games_year as Number: TS emits -1,0,1,2 instead of 1900-2012 -> queries filtering games_year>=2000 return empty (FN) or wrong (FP).
height/weight as Number: negatives and 0/1 values -> implausible; queries with height>180 or weight between 60 and 80 mostly miss.
age as Number: -1..2 -> age>20 filters return empty.

FK columns (games_id, person_id, city_id, sport_id, event_id, competitor_id, medal_id, region_id) draw from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement; since parent PKs collapse to few survivors, FK fan-out is skewed and many child rows reference the same tiny parent set.
No-PK tables (games_city, person_region, competitor_event) keep all drawn rows including duplicates -> duplicate-tie queries (COUNT DISTINCT vs COUNT) may behave differently than original.
String fuzzer on noc/region_name: joins on region_name equality still work (same gibberish reused via literal pool) but LIKE '%...%' patterns from gold literals rarely match -> FN.
medal_name 'NA' vs 'Gold'/'Silver'/'Bronze': TS String replaces with random strings; queries filtering medal_name='Gold' return empty unless literal pool seeds it.

Literal pool from train SQL will inject some real values (e.g. 'Gold', 'Summer', 'M', 'F', years) into samplers, partially rescuing enum/year columns; p=0.2 fresh-draw probability keeps some real values.
